findings.evidence: Description: "digested on-bead with trypsin". SDRF comment[cleavage agent details]: "NT=Lys-C;AC=MS:1001309" in every row.
findings.explanation: The description says the enzyme was trypsin, but the SDRF records Lys-C. A database search configured from the SDRF would use the wrong cleavage specificity, which would hurt peptide identification and quantification.
findings.suggested_fix: Set comment[cleavage agent details] to trypsin (NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251) in all rows. If Lys-C was actually used as well, correct the description instead.

findings.evidence: Rule check: "4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N." Description: "12 samples ... one TMTpro 16-plex kit ... Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: The 12 samples use TMT126 to TMT132N, which leaves 4 of the 16 TMTpro channels empty. This matches the description, so it is expected and has no effect on the analysis. The empty channels should simply be excluded from quantification. The likely cause is that the design has only 12 samples, so the kit was not filled.
findings.suggested_fix: No change to the SDRF is needed. Note in the study documentation that these four channels were intentionally left empty.

summary: One metadata mismatch: the SDRF lists Lys-C as the cleavage agent while the description says trypsin. The four unused TMTpro channels are consistent with the 12-sample design in the description, so I have only explained that rule warning. Everything else the description covers (organism, cell line, disease, compound, antibody, 12 samples) agrees with the SDRF.
